title: Kirby's postwar band falling apart; trying Bud Powell
summary: Procope closes his earlier answer, then says the postwar Kirby band was thrown together like a jam session; Kirby was bewildered and even tried Bud Powell on piano at a rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: That's the only answer. I mean I've been asked that question and I've given it a lot of thought. That's all I can think about it. That's all.
And now what about the Kirby band? What did it feel like coming back to Kirby? It was far from what it had been.

Well, again I say I didn't like it at all. I didn't like it at all. At that time, when I came back, it was just like joining an outfit that was just thrown together and, you know, just like a jam session, let's put it that way. You know, it wasn't my recollection of the Kirby band, this beautiful music we used to play, and it wasn't the same scene. It was a different scene entirely.
Was there a change in him? It's always said that he was sort of almost despairing there, because everything just seemed to sort of fall apart.

Oh, of course, that's right. That's right. It was a situation that he could not cope with. He himself just didn't know which way to turn. He was just bewildered. He tried and tried and tried, the best he could, to build it back up again, but he just couldn't.
Then again, you must remember that, like we were just talking about the be-bops. See the be-bop people were taking over, in a way of speaking, and he even tried some

of those be-boppers, see. He tried everything and you know, he had a -- I remember he had a rehearsal one time, when I first came out of the Army, and he had -- the piano player he had at rehearsal, what's this famous be-bop piano player's name?
That's right. He had Bud Powell on piano, you know, so he tried the best he could. But he couldn't bring it off.
